channel.title: Vatican News - English
channel.description: News from the Vatican - News about the Church

item.title: Canadian Bishop: When does state neutrality threaten one’s religious freedom?
item.description:
Following new instructions barring military chaplains from referencing God in certain contexts, Bishop Scott McCaig speaks to Vatican News about the dangerous precedence this policy can set, the road that led to these instructions, an inter-faith committee dedicated to confronting this policy, and the hope that Canadian Catholics have.

Read all

item.title: Congress of Scholas Chairs reflects on challenges of AI
item.description:
Scholars, politicians, businessmen and women, religious leaders, activists, and young people are gathering in Indonesia to reflect on “one of the great challenges of our time: how to ensure that artificial intelligence is at the service of human dignity, fraternity, and peace.”

Read all

item.title: Catholics, Copts, Muslims: Latin Bishop of Alexandria on Christianity in Egypt
item.description:
The Latin Apostolic Vicar of Alexandria speaks to Vatican News about the Catholic Church in Egypt, its relations with the Coptic Orthodox and Muslim communities, and the ongoing conflict in Gaza.

Read all

item.title: Pope receives Latvian President Edgars Rinkēvičs
item.description:
Pope Leo XIV receives the President of the Republic of Latvia, Mr Edgars Rinkēvičs, in audience in the Vatican.

Read all

item.title: Bishop Daibes: International pressure needed to protect Palestinians in the Holy Land
item.description:
Bishop Jamal Daibes, Bishop of Djibouti and Apostolic Administrator of Somalia, shines the spotlight on the region and calls for international and diplomatic pressure to protect Palestinians in the Holy Land and enable them to remain in their homeland with dignity, freedom and security.

Read all

item.title: Cardinal Hollerich: Robert Schuman, a man from the borders who built Europe
item.description:
Pope Leo XIV’s upcoming Apostolic Journey to France will also bring him to Metz where Robert Schuman, one of the founders of the European Union, grew up. Cardinal Jean-Claude Hollerich, Archbishop of Luxembourg, reflects on this important figure and how his experience of living in border areas shaped his political action and ideas.

Read all

item.title: Pope to Oxford’s Oriel College: Seek truth, promote integral anthropology
item.description:
Pope Leo XIV meets with members of the Oriel College of Oxford University, and invites them to look to St. John Henry Newman as an example of the inseparability of faith and reason.

Read all

item.title: When children go hungry
item.description:
As some international aid groups leave Ethiopia, Church-run assistance programs, like those supported by the Catholic Near East Welfare Association, continue to feed children who cry from hunger.

Read all

item.title: Primate of Colombia: Before rebuilding Churches, we must rebuild the people
item.description:
Following the earthquake that affected numerous communities in western Colombia, Cardinal Luis José Rueda Aparicio, the Primate of the country, tells Vatican News about the "Spiritual First Aid" - a support mission of 4 bishops and 80 priests who set out to accompany the suffering in the impacted areas.

Read all

item.title: Caritas Internationalis on Nepal: ‘We must all face the climate chaos'
item.description:
Following recent flash flooding, Caritas Nepal is ramping up its aid to be able to reach up to 4,000 families. Caritas Internationalis Secretary General calls on the global community to “commit to do what is necessary to care for our common home.”

Read all

item.title: Pope: Amid conflict, Church must bear witness to service and hope
item.description:
As he meets with Latin-rite Bishops from Arab regions, Pope Leo XIV urges the Church to confront conflict and division with solidarity for the poor and bear witness that it is possible to live and hope together.

Read all

item.title: Pope Leo to seminarians: Learn to remain with Jesus
item.description:
“The heart of the seminary experience” is “learning to be with the Master, Jesus,” Pope Leo XIV tells Italian seminarians from the Pius XI Regional Seminary in Molfetta and the Episcopal Seminary of Aversa.

Read all

item.title: Salzburg Youth Orchestra performs with Mozart's violins in the Vatican
item.description:
After meeting with Pope Leo, the Salzburg Youth Orchestra "Bella Musica" recorded a concert in the historic Vatican Radio studio in the Vatican Gardens, using the two original Mozart violins. The Austrian composer once played for a Pope in Rome more than 250 years ago.

Read all

item.title: Haitian bishop concerned over end of US protected status for immigrants
item.description:
Bishop Pierre-André Dumas of Anse-à-Veau-Miragoâne, expresses his concern for Haitian immigrants in the US, following the termination of Temporary Protected Status (TPS) for them. TPS is a measure designed to welcome and protect people from countries where wars, natural disasters, and serious humanitarian crises make it impossible to return them safely.

Read all

item.title: Timor-Leste welcomes home mortal remains of bishops who stood with the people
item.description:
The mortal remains of three former Church leaders return to Dili, joining those of a fourth bishop as Timor-Leste honours pastors who accompanied the nation through some of its darkest chapters.

Read all

item.title: Pope speaks with Colombia’s President following devastating earthquake
item.description:
Pope Leo XIV speaks by telephone with the Colombian President, expressing his solidarity following the country’s recent earthquake.

Read all

item.title: New Bishops gather in Rome for formation course
item.description:
Some 147 newly appointed bishops from five continents are taking part in a Vatican formation course addressing mission, pastoral ministry, safeguarding, liturgy and Church governance, culminating in an audience with Pope Leo XIV.

Read all

item.title: AI will provide ‘an explosion of creativity, but brakes are needed’
item.description:
As the Vatican hosts a conference exploring how technology is changing art, culture, and the human mind, organizers reflect on the need for prudence when approaching the creative boost that artificial intelligence offers humanity.

Read all

item.title: Holy See to UN: Nuclear testing harms more than one generation
item.description:
On the International Day Against Nuclear Tests on September 1, the Counselor and Chargé d'Affaires at the Holy See Mission to the United Nations renews the Holy See’s appeal to end nuclear testing and stresses how interconnected a nuclear-free world is to establishing “a just and lasting peace.”

Read all

item.title: Dicastery Prefect urges Philippine religious to be prophets of peace
item.description:
Sr. Simona Brambilla, Prefect of the Dicastery for Institutes of Consecrated Life and Societies of Apostolic Life, invites consecrated women and men gathered in Zamboanga, Philippines, to recognize God in the vulnerable and become witnesses of peace in a wounded world.

Read all

item.title: Poland: parents and bishops oppose changes to religious education rules
item.description:
Poland’s new rules on religion classes in public schools are raising concerns among parents, catechists and bishops, who say the changes could make it more difficult for students to attend.

Read all

item.title: Zambia: Bishops’ Conference launches the 2026 Season of Creation
item.description:
The Zambia Conference of Catholic Bishops (ZCCB) has officially launched the 2026 Season of Creation, calling on Zambians to protect the environment and stand up for communities affected by climate change.

Read all

item.title: Care for Creation is a theological question
item.description:
The document “Caring for Our Common Home” calls for a “responsible and fraternal response to the Triune God”. The ecological question is a theological question: the way we care for Creation reveals and shapes our relationship with God. The deterioration of the environment is alarming and urgent action is needed to ensure the sustainability of the planet. Everything is connected: we must listen to the cry of the Earth and the cry of the poor.

Read all

item.title: Mission of hope in education: A missionary from Congo in Italy
item.description:
African women are quietly renewing the Church in places where faith first arrived on their shores, as the Global South gives back while vocations decline in parts of the West. Through education, presence, and prayer, religious sisters like Sr. Julie Eyaya, CSF, offer a witness of love lived daily in the field of education.

Read all

item.title: Book on death-row ministry praised by Pope Francis released in English
item.description:
“A Christian on Death Row,” a book by American lay chaplain Dale Recinella recounting his ministry among prisoners condemned to death, is now available in English.

Read all

item.title: Pope at Audience: Church is called to serve humanity, unmask society's contradictions
item.description:
At the Wednesday General Audience, Pope Leo XIV reflects on the Church’s mission to be at the service of humanity by engaging with reality, getting involved in the challenges of our time, and bearing witness to Christ.

Read all

item.title: Pope Leo: ‘It is not yet too late’ to turn destruction into life
item.description:
Pope Leo XIV encourages Christians to embrace ecological conversion, transform destruction into life, and renew their commitment to caring for creation and the poor.

Read all

item.title: Pope’s September prayer intention: ‘For the care of water’
item.description:
Pope Leo XIV invites everyone to pray for “the care of water” during September as Christians celebrate the Season of Creation.

Read all

item.title: Season of Creation begins with worldwide prayer for our common home
item.description:
Christians around the world mark the 11th World Day of Prayer for the Care of Creation, launching a month-long ecumenical season of prayer and action for the environment.

Read all

item.title: Cardinal Ouellet wins case against woman who accused him of abuse
item.description:
A ruling by the Superior Court of Quebec in Canada finds that Cardinal Marc Ouellet was “falsely accused” of sexual assault in connection with a class action against the Archdiocese of Quebec, and he will receive $100,000 in damages, which he will donate to organizations combating the sexual abuse of Indigenous peoples.

Read all

item.title: Mozambique: Cathedral of Beira hosts Day for Catechists
item.description:
Over the weekend, the Archdiocese of Beira in Mozambique hosted catechists of the diocese for Catechist Day. The Mass was presided over by Bishop Antonio Manuel Bogaio Constantino, M.C.C.I. He is the Bishop of Caia Diocese and the Apostolic Administrator of Beira. Several priests concelebrated.

Read all

item.title: Missionary in Haiti: 'Violence cannot discourage us'
item.description:
Maddalena Boschetti, a fidei donum missionary in Haiti since 2002, tells Vatican News how remaining in the violence-stricken country and supporting those in need when all hope seems lost is a way to respond to the violence itself.

Read all

item.title: Cardinal Czerny: 25 years of gatherings in ‘service of the Amazon'
item.description:
In a message to participants of 25th Inter-Institutional Meeting of the Amazonian Itinerant Team, Cardinal Michael Czerny stresses the importance of reflecting on the work of various institutions for the spiritual, physical, and human wellbeing of the Amazon over the last two and a half decades.

Read all

item.title: Pope receives the oversight commission of the ‘House for the Relief of Suffering’
item.description:
During a meeting on 31 August at Castel Gandolfo, the oversight commission for the 'House for the Relief of Suffering' - a research hospital founded by St Pio of Pietrelcina - was able to share with Leo XIV the work it has done since it was established last May.

Read all

item.title: Iceland: The Arctic gateway that remains closed to Europe
item.description:
Just over 52% of Icelanders vote against resuming negotiations on European Union membership. The referendum highlights an important divide within the country: between rural areas, where the “No” vote prevailed, and the capital, where the majority voted for “Yes”.

Read all

item.title: Bishop of Datong ordained in China
item.description:
Appointed Bishop of Datong (Shanxi, China) by Pope Leo XIV on August 10, following the approval of his candidacy under the framework of the Provisional Agreement between the Holy See and the People’s Republic of China, Paolo Liu Honggang receives episcopal consecration.

Read all

item.title: Nuncio to Romania: Pope John Paul I is an example of reconciliation
item.description:
On August 30, the Apostolic Nuncio to Romania and the Republic of Moldova celebrated Mass at the Church of the Most Holy Redeemer in Bucharest and the Vatican Foundation “John Paul I” donated an icon and a relic of Blessed Albino Luciani to this church known as the “Italian Church.”

Read all

item.title: Bishop celebrates centenary of first Catholic Mass in Svalbard, Norway
item.description:
Bishop Erik Varden of Trondheim and Apostolic Administrator of Tromsø celebrated a solemn Mass in Longyearbyen on Sunday, 30 August, to mark 100 years since the first Catholic Mass was celebrated in Svalbard, Norway. In his homily, Bishop Varden reflects on vulnerability and loneliness, calling Christians to rediscover a sound sense of reality and to bring Christ’s reconciliation, healing and friendship to those who are isolated and afraid.

Read all

item.title: Stop the massacres and mass kidnappings, Nigerian bishops appeal as bandits attack Mosques
item.description:
“The latest barbaric abduction of more than 60 worshippers from a Mosque in Borgu, Niger State, and the horrific massacre of 47 innocent citizens, with another 17 people seriously injured in Ukum, Benue State, represent a further deterioration of the security situation.” The bleak assessment was made by Archbishop Matthew Man-Oso Ndagoso, the Archbishop of Kaduna and President of the Catholic Bishops’ Conference of Nigeria (CBCN).

Read all

item.title: Pope Leo urges release of Haiti hostages, aid for Nepal after deadly floods
item.description:
Following the recitation of the midday Angelus prayer from Castel Gandolfo on Sunday, Pope Leo XIV condemned the recent massacre in Haiti, made an urgent appeal for the release of hostages, and renewed his call for concrete assistance to Nepal following devastating floods and mudslides that have killed hundreds and left thousands missing.

Read all

item.title: Pope at Angelus: Even when confused like Peter, dialogue with the Lord
item.description:
During his Sunday Angelus address in Castel Gandolfo, Pope Leo XIV reminds the faithful that St. Peter was very human and that, like him, we ought to “humbly tell Jesus what we truly feel, even when our hearts are confused."

Read all

item.title: Archbishop Gallagher: The Holy See pursues a diplomacy that believes in peace
item.description:
At the end of his mission to Moscow, the Holy See's Secretary for Relations with States and International Organizations, Archbishop Paul Richard Gallagher, speaks to Vatican News about his journey.

Read all

item.title: During procession on Lake Albano, Pope entrusts wounded children to Mary
item.description:
Pope Leo XIV arrived by boat at the beach on Lake Albano, where a Marian procession that began at the Church of Mary Most Holy of the Lake had come to an end. The Holy Father, travelling aboard the Falco, which was decorated with yellow and white flowers, joined the faithful gathered on the shore and led them in prayer to the Virgin Mary.

Read all

item.title: Pope: Do not give in to hatred; do not let evil disfigure humanity
item.description:
In his homily for Mass in Castel Gandolfo, Pope Leo XIV reflects on the beauty of “simple gestures” of devotion and emphasizes that, in a world that dismisses forgiveness as naive, believing in God can become a pathway toward peace. After Mass, the Holy Father made history by embarking on a boat on Lake Albano to take part in the procession for the Feast of Our Lady of the Lake.

Read all

item.title: Pope Leo grants Eastern Synods the faculty to remove Patriarchs
item.description:
With an Apostolic Letter issued motu proprio on 29 August, Pope Leo XIV provides the Synods of Bishops of Eastern Catholic Churches the faculty to remove their respective Patriarchs in order “to restore the wounded communion, even by removing him from office for grave cause”, in the event their “bond” is “irreparably compromised.” In such an event, the Roman Pontiff must grant assent to the Synod’s judgment.

Read all

item.title: In wake of devastating floods, Pope sends aid to Nepal
item.description:
Through the Dicastery for the Service of Charity, Pope Leo XIV has sent financial support to Caritas Nepal as relief operations continue and the death toll in the affected regions rises hourly, with over 630 known to have died and approximately 3,000 still missing.

Read all

item.title: Pope Leo XIV to make history with Marian procession on Lake Albano
item.description:
Pope Leo XIV will celebrate tonight the Feast of Our Lady of the Lake in Castel Gandolfo at the church consecrated by Pope Saint Paul VI and will become the first Pope to travel by boat along part of the lake, accompanied by around ten other vessels.

Read all

item.title: 'As St. Augustine teaches, may the Church be a community open for all'
item.description:
Cardinal Rolandas Makrickas, Archpriest of the Papal Basilica of Saint Mary Major, presiding over Mass in Rome on 28 August for the liturgical memorial of Saint Augustine, Bishop of Hippo, reflects on the spiritual journey of the “Doctor of Grace,” who “deeply loved the Church” and never tired of serving it.

Read all

item.title: Lord's Day Reflection: 'Not conformed but transformed’
item.description:
As the Church celebrates the Twenty-Second Sunday in Ordinary Time, Fr. Edmund Power reflects on the theme: “Not conformed but transformed.”

Read all

item.title: US Bishop calls on international community to assist victims of Nepal flooding
item.description:
The Chairman of the USCCB’s Committee on International Justice and Peace, Bishop A. Elias Zaidan, calls on the international community “to mobilize greater humanitarian assistance support” for victims of deadly flash flooding in Nepal.

Read all
